title: Graded SLI Contracts and Eviction Prioritization for Multi-Region Model Endpoints
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary:
This ticket defines a scheme for graded SLI/SLO contracts per endpoint and model variant, an eviction/priority policy for load-shedding across tenants and regions, and operational thresholds that will drive circuit breakers and multi-region failover. The goal is to provide deterministic, auditable behavior when capacity is constrained while preserving the best possible user experience for high-priority customers.

Scope:
- Define canonical SLIs for model endpoints (availability, p50/p95/p99 latency, request success, model-quality drift) with measurement rules and tag conventions.
- Introduce graded SLO buckets (Platinum/Gold/Silver/Bronze) with explicit error budget policies and automated remediation actions.
- Define error-budget burn detection windows and automated remediation: soft-throttle, model-variant fallback, regional failover.
- Define circuit-breaker state machine for endpoints and model-variants with thresholds, cooldowns, and manual override hooks.
- Produce an eviction/prioritization matrix used by the scheduler to evict requests or degrade quality under overload (per-tenant weight, pinned variants, paid tiers).
- Deliverables: SLI spec doc, example SLO manifest for 3 representative endpoints, automation playbook (alerts -> actions), unit tests + e2e simulation harness, docs for SRE/PM/SE.

Canonical SLIs (measurement guidance):
1) Request Success Rate (availability): fraction of requests that return a 2xx structured response within max_time_ms (defined per route). Measure by route + region + variant.
 - Primary metric: success_count / total_count over rolling window.
2) Tail Latency: p95 and p99 of server-side end-to-end latency (ingress -> last token emitted) excluding streaming idle time.
 - Tags: route, model_variant, region, batch_size_bucket.
3) Quality SLI (model correctness/stability): daily aggregated EvalSet semantic-similarity >= threshold OR automated BLEU/ROUGE/proxy metric for deterministic tasks.
 - For chat/generation endpoints, use calibrated automated classifier + periodic human audits for drift detection.
4) Resource-side throttles: fraction of requests actively rate-limited or rejected due to circuit-breaker open. We label these as "policy rejections" and treat them separately for customer-level reporting.

Graded SLO tiers (example):
- Platinum: Availability >= 99.95% (monthly); p99 latency <= 400ms; Quality drift tolerance 0.5% monthly. Error budget: 0.05% monthly.
- Gold: Availability >= 99.5%; p99 <= 700ms; Quality drift tolerance 1% monthly.
- Silver: Availability >= 99.0%; p99 <= 1200ms.
- Bronze: Availability >= 98.0%; p99 <= 2000ms.
(These are starting points to be validated against production telemetry and customer SLAs.)

Error budget policy and automated responses:
- Burn detection windows: short (5m), medium (1h), long (24h). A burn alarm triggers when burn_rate > X for the window (configurable per tier).
- Automated remediation ladders (example for Gold endpoints):
  1) Short window spike (>5m): scale up burst capacity if available, enable aggressive batching tuning for new requests, mark feature flags for reduced max_tokens by 20% for Bronze traffic.
  2) Sustained medium window (>1h): divert Bronze and free-tier traffic to quantized variant (q4/q8) or to cold-cache responses; enable regional request shedding rules.
  3) Sustained long window (>24h) with error budget exhausted: initiate regional failover for high-priority customers, notify account owners, and open incident.
- Error budget banking/borrowing: allow short-term borrow from next window if compensated by a planned reclamation policy (automatic throttles or scheduled capacity add). Borrowing must be logged and subject to audit.

Circuit breaker state machine (summary):
- States: CLOSED -> ALLOWED traffic; HALF_OPEN -> limited test traffic; OPEN -> reject if policy rejects; FORCED_OPEN -> manual emergency open; FORCED_CLOSE -> manual override to ignore checks.
- Entry conditions to OPEN: route error_rate >= 8% for 3 consecutive 1-minute buckets OR p99_latency >= 2x SLO threshold for 5 minutes.
- HALF_OPEN flow: allow a small percentage (configurable per tier, default 2%) of traffic, verify success rate over 2 minutes, then promote to CLOSED or re-open.
- Cooldown: minimum 10 minutes before auto-transition from OPEN->HALF_OPEN.

Multi-region failover triggers and rules:
- Failover should be prioritized by customer tier and pinned-variant policies. Default strategy: route -> local_region -> same-region fallback variant -> different-region failover.
- Trigger conditions for auto failover: local region median host failure rate > 20% AND error budget for region exhausted OR sustained degradation for >15 minutes.
- Failover TTL: 30 minutes by default; health-checked automatically every 2 minutes.
- Drift protection: do not failover customers with pinned regional deployment without manual approval.

Eviction and load-shedding priority matrix (scheduler inputs):
- Keys: customer_tier (Platinum/Gold/Silver/Bronze), pinned_variant (true/false), realtime_priority (urgent/normal/batch), feature_flags (safety_mode), cost_profile (high/low).
- Eviction ordering (lowest to highest priority): anonymous/free -> Bronze non-pinned batch -> Silver normal -> Gold normal -> Platinum pinned -> Platinum urgent.
- Degradation steps before hard reject: reduce max_tokens by 30% -> switch to quantized variant -> reduce concurrent tokens per request -> reject Bronze traffic.

Operational runbook & observability:
- Dashboards: per-route SLI widget (p50/p95/p99), error-budget burn chart, per-tenant deviation leaderboard, circuit-breaker heatmap. Link: https://dashboards.redwood.ai/d/runtime-resilience/sli-overview
- Alerts: PagerDuty for Platinum SLO breaches; Slack for Gold; email for Silver/Bronze. Alerting rules included in playbook.
- Audit logs: every automated remediation step must create an audit event with reason, timestamp, actor (automation), and current error-budget state. Audit events stored in BigQuery and view in console.

Testing and rollout plan:
1) Unit tests for SLI calculations + mocks for bucketed latency.
2) Simulation: use historical traffic replay with induced degradation to validate remediation ladders (ENG-302412 will own the simulation harness PR).
3) Canary release: roll SLO enforcement to 5% of traffic for non-critical routes, collect metrics for 2 weeks.
4) Gradual rollout with verification gates and documented rollback steps.

Open questions / trade-offs:
- Quality SLI automation: what threshold metrics provide reliable signal for semantic drift without large false positives? We propose to couple automated signals with weekly human review for the first 90d.
- Borrowing policy: how aggressive can borrowing be before it undermines customer trust? Recommend strict limits for Platinum accounts.
- Latency SLI for streaming endpoints: p99 is less meaningful for streaming; should we track token-level latency (first-token, average token delta) instead?
